clue.text: Company support for office machine

blocks.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company
a pier is a column supporting a bridge or arch

explanation.surface: A firm is backing the purchase of some new equipment for its office.
explanation.definitionFit: A photocopier, usually just called a copier, is a standard piece of office equipment.

clue.text: Runs into kind of driver liable to have road rage?

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a cabby is a taxi driver

explanation.surface: A cab driver prone to road rage crashes into others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of driver' looks like part of the definition, but it is the wordplay; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabby means irritable and bad-tempered, the sort of person who might fly off the handle in traffic.

clue.text: Under pressure, infer changes in goal for foreign correspondent?

indicators.note: in a down entry, the rest sits under the first letter, so the pieces stack in order
changes means the letters are altered into a new order

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure
the letters of this word, shuffled
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper under pressure draws conclusions about a reporter abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign correspondent' suggests a journalist overseas; the question mark signals a letter-writer in another country.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen pal writes letters to someone, often in another country, so is literally a correspondent from abroad.

clue.text: Going without info that's urgent

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one word wraps round another

blocks.note: an exit is a going out, a departure
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Leaving without information on something pressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like lacking, but here it has its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent describes something pressing that demands immediate attention.

clue.text: Secure with cable and pull back, producing mess on warship

indicators.note: going back means the words are read from the end towards the start

to draw is to pull

explanation.surface: Sailors tie up the ship and haul in lines, causing a mess on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess' looks like disorder after the work, but it is a naval dining room.
explanation.definitionFit: The wardroom is the officers' dining and living quarters on a naval vessel, their mess.

clue.text: Adjusted rent over a time within existing option

indicators.note: adjusted means altered, so the letters are rearranged
in a down entry, a piece over another simply comes first
within puts the pieces inside another word

blocks.note: something alive is existing
the letters of this word, shuffled
taken as written

explanation.surface: A landlord's revised rent is offered as the current choice.
explanation.definitionFit: An alternative is another possibility to choose, an option.

clue.text: Sea-creature in hold moving around quietly

blocks.note: taken as written, for the shuffle

explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but belongs to the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolphin is a marine mammal, a creature of the sea.

clue.text: Hatred in speaker's position after losing power at the top

blocks.note: a speaker stands on a podium

explanation.definitionFit: Odium is general or widespread hatred and disgust directed at someone.

clue.text: Popular newcomer turned up within my smaller group

within puts these pieces inside another word

blocks.note: taken as written
something in is fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: A well-liked new arrival appears among my small band.
explanation.definitionFit: A minority is the smaller part of a group, outnumbered by the rest.

clue.text: A loose woman in family

blocks.note: taken as written
to loose is to untie or set free

explanation.surface: A promiscuous woman lurks within someone's household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose woman' reads as one phrase, but 'loose' is a verb here, and the definition starts at 'woman'.
explanation.definitionFit: An auntie, an affectionate form of aunt, is a female relative: a parent's sister.

clue.text: Part of stable with one working horse

blocks.note: a stall is one compartment of a stable
I is the Roman numeral for one
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: In a stable compartment stands a single horse put to work.
explanation.definitionFit: A stallion is an uncastrated adult male horse, kept for breeding.

clue.text: Who needs skill to break up drunken rampage?

definitions.text: Who needs skill to break up drunken rampage?

indicators.note: breaking up something splits it open, so another piece goes into the middle

blocks.note: a bender is a drinking spree
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: Someone must step in skilfully to stop a riot of drunks.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: the person behind the bar needs tact to stop a drinking session getting out of hand. A bender is slang for a drinking binge.
explanation.definitionFit: The person serving drinks in a pub is often the first to deal with drunken customers getting out of hand.

clue.text: People on board created riot at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so the letters are in disarray

blocks.note: taken as written, for the shuffle

explanation.surface: Passengers on a ship cause a riot out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' and 'at sea' suggest a ship; the board is a company's board of directors.
explanation.definitionFit: A directorate is a company's board of directors, the people who sit on the board.

clue.text: All-round sporting achievement for an American poet of old

definitions.note: the poet is Greek; 'an American' belongs to the first meaning

blocks.note: first meaning: in American baseball, a home run, where the batter runs all the way round the bases
second meaning: the ancient Greek poet of the Iliad and the Odyssey

explanation.surface: An ancient poet is credited with an all-round sporting feat in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For an American' attaches to the sporting meaning: homer is American slang for a home run in baseball.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer is the epic poet of ancient Greece, and in baseball a homer is a home run.

clue.text: Prepare to watch circus, including bizarre main show

indicators.note: something bizarre is strange and out of shape, so these letters are jumbled
including means the circus word holds the jumbled letters inside it

blocks.note: you enter the theatre or arena when you are about to watch
a circus performs under a big tent
the letters of this word, shuffled

explanation.surface: Getting ready to see a circus whose main act is strange.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled word sits between the T and the ENT of the tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A show is a performance put on to amuse an audience, which is what entertainment is.

clue.text: For instance, repeatedly ringing king with evidence of debts — shocking

indicators.note: repeatedly tells you to use the same short piece twice in a row
ringing means encircling another piece

the same abbreviation again, as told
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: A king's repeated debts are scandalous.
explanation.definitionFit: Egregious means outstandingly bad, shocking in its awfulness.

clue.text: Asian vessel's short journey — it carries second-hand stuff

blocks.note: a junk is a Chinese sailing ship
taken as written
a hop is a short trip

explanation.surface: A Chinese ship's brief voyage carrying used goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carries' suggests a ship's cargo; a shop carries stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A junk shop stocks cheap used goods and bric-a-brac for sale.

clue.text: Hear I've tangled with dunce? Right, he could do better

taken as written, for the shuffle

explanation.surface: A teacher overhears a muddled dunce and concludes the pupil could do better.
explanation.walkthrough: The R from 'Right' joins the anagram fodder too.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Could do better' is the classic school report comment on a pupil who is not working to their potential.

clue.text: Literary event for English university town

blocks.note: first meaning: an event where an author reads aloud from their work
second meaning: a town in Berkshire with a university

explanation.surface: A book event is staged in an English college town.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading is a large town west of London with a university, and a reading is a public literary recital.

clue.text: Part in Chekhov — is it originally for one in company?

explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' and 'company' suggest a theatre role and troupe; company here means guests.
explanation.definitionFit: Having company means having guests, so a visitor is one member of that company.

clue.text: Spread the rumour, initially, in all directions

in places those letters inside another piece

blocks.note: S, E, W and N are the four compass points
the opening letters of these two words

explanation.definitionFit: Strewn means scattered, spread untidily over an area.

clue.text: Critical article covering North African country

explanation.walkthrough: 'North African country' reads as one phrase, but North is just the letter N; the country is in East Africa.

clue.text: Cautiously proceeded to signal agreement about state's borders

blocks.note: a nod signals agreement
the first and last letters of this word

clue.text: Express sadness in public for error

blocks.note: a sigh expresses sadness

explanation.surface: Showing grief openly is a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is a mistake made through failing to notice something.

clue.text: Doctor has plot outside current medical facility

explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' fits the medical surface so well that it hides its job as the anagram signal.

clue.text: Husband absorbed in a big book, comfortable and relaxed

blocks.note: a tome is a big, heavy book

explanation.surface: A husband is engrossed in a hefty book, comfortable and at ease.

E is the abbreviation for English

blocks.note: PR, public relations, is publicity
taken as written
